title: The Atmosphere The Wise Services Of Clouds Wind Rain Lightning And Thunder

questions.question: Who is being spoken to by the atmosphere at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: A traveler who is living in the world as a guest.

questions.question: What does the atmosphere invite the traveler to do?
questions.answer: It calls him to pay attention to it so he can find the One he is searching for.

questions.question: How is the face of the atmosphere described in two different ways?
questions.answer: It is described as harsh in one way but also gentle and helpful.

questions.question: Give two important jobs of the clouds mentioned in the passage.
questions.answer: They water the earth and bring life-giving water to living things.

questions.question: How do the clouds show discipline and obedience?
questions.answer: They disappear and return quickly, as if following commands right away.

questions.question: What happens when the order for rain is given?
questions.answer: The clouds gather very quickly and fill the sky, ready for the next command.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice about the air and its tiny parts?
questions.answer: He sees them acting in an organized way, as if carrying out many orders.

questions.question: Name three things the air helps carry or provide.
questions.answer: It helps provide breath, heat and light, and it also carries sound.

questions.question: How does the passage connect wind to plant life?
questions.answer: It says the air helps plants by assisting with pollination.

questions.question: Why is rain called “mercy” in the passage?
questions.answer: Because each drop brings many kind and helpful gifts for living things.

questions.question: What does the traveler understand about the raindrops besides their usefulness?
questions.answer: He sees that they are delicate, shining, sweet, and full of care.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice about lightning and thunder?
questions.answer: He sees that they also have amazing tasks and are not meaningless events.

questions.question: What main idea about nature is taught through clouds, wind, rain, and lightning?
questions.answer: They all work with wisdom and purpose, showing that they are under the control of Allah.

questions.question: At the start of the passage, what place begins to “speak” to the traveler?
questions.answer: The space around the earth, the atmosphere.

questions.question: What is the traveler trying to discover through what he sees?
questions.answer: He is trying to find the One who sent him into the world.

questions.question: What feeling do the thunderclaps give along with their power?
questions.answer: They bring both awe and joy.

questions.question: In what way do the clouds serve the earth with wisdom and mercy?
questions.answer: They send water where it is needed and help keep life going.

questions.question: How do the clouds help with temperature?
questions.answer: They reduce excessive heat in a beneficial way.

questions.question: What comparison is used to explain how clouds appear and disappear?
questions.answer: They are compared to a trained army that moves according to orders.

questions.question: How fast do the clouds gather when it is time for rain?
questions.answer: They gather within a very short time, even just minutes.

questions.question: What does the ordered work of the air suggest to the traveler?
questions.answer: It suggests that the air is being directed by the ruler of the universe.

questions.question: Besides helping living things breathe, what else does the air transmit?
questions.answer: It carries sound and delivers things like heat, light, and electricity.

questions.question: What does the description of raindrops show about their source?
questions.answer: It shows that they come as gifts from a hidden store of mercy.

questions.question: What idea is repeated through the examples of clouds, air, and rain?
questions.answer: That these things do not act on their own but serve a wise purpose.

questions.question: How does the passage lead the reader to think about thunder and lightning?
questions.answer: It presents them as meaningful parts of the same carefully managed system.

questions.question: What conclusion can be drawn about the natural world from this passage?
questions.answer: Nature is not random; it is arranged and controlled with wisdom and compassion.

questions.question: Why does the atmosphere call out to the traveler in the passage?
questions.answer: To guide him toward knowing the One behind creation.

questions.question: What does the traveler do after the atmosphere calls him?
questions.answer: He looks closely and listens carefully to what is happening in it.

questions.question: What does the passage say the clouds provide for the people and creatures of the earth?
questions.answer: They provide the water needed for life.

questions.question: How do the clouds act in a way that points to order instead of chaos?
questions.answer: They withdraw completely at times and then quickly return when needed.

questions.question: What does the phrase about waiting for further orders show about the clouds?
questions.answer: It shows that they are presented as obedient and controlled.

questions.question: What does the traveler see in the movement and work of the wind?
questions.answer: He sees wisdom, generosity, and careful organization.

questions.question: Why is it surprising that the air performs so many jobs?
questions.answer: Because it is made of lifeless matter, yet it acts as if it is following exact instructions.

questions.question: How does the air help both animals and plants?
questions.answer: It supports breathing for living creatures and helps plants reproduce.

questions.question: What is special about the raindrops in the passage besides their appearance?
questions.answer: They carry many blessings and useful purposes within them.

questions.question: What does the image of mercy taking shape in drops help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader see rain as a direct sign of care and kindness.

questions.question: What does the traveler learn from looking at lightning and listening to thunder?
questions.answer: He learns that they too are used for meaningful and amazing purposes.

questions.question: Which is a better summary of the passage: “Nature runs itself” or “Nature is directed”? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: “Nature is directed,” because the passage keeps showing order, service, and response to command.

questions.question: What character of Allah is especially reflected in the description of rain?
questions.answer: His mercy.

questions.question: Who is the main human figure in this passage?
questions.answer: A thoughtful traveler observing the world.

questions.question: What message does the atmosphere give him?
questions.answer: It tells him to study it in order to find the One he seeks.

questions.question: How are thunderclaps described emotionally in the passage?
questions.answer: They are strong and frightening in one sense, but also cheerful and uplifting.

questions.question: What do the clouds do for the “garden of the world”?
questions.answer: They water it and help keep it alive.

questions.question: What does the passage say about how clouds respond when help is needed?
questions.answer: They hurry to bring assistance wherever it is required.

questions.question: What detail shows that the clouds can become hidden completely?
questions.answer: The passage says they can vanish so fully that no sign of them remains.

questions.question: What military image is used for the clouds, and what does it mean?
questions.answer: They are likened to a trained army, meaning they move in strict discipline.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice about the work of the air in the atmosphere?
questions.answer: It carries out many tasks in an orderly and beneficial way.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the tiny particles of air?
questions.answer: To show that even the smallest parts seem to serve a command and purpose.

questions.question: How does the air benefit communication and life?
questions.answer: It helps living things survive and also carries sound.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying rain comes from a hidden treasury?
questions.answer: It suggests rain is a precious gift sent with care from Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: Why is “mercy” a fitting name for rain according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because rain brings many blessings and supports life with kindness.

questions.question: What broad lesson is taught by the final mention of thunder and lightning?
questions.answer: Even dramatic natural events have wise purposes in Allah’s creation.

questions.question: What role does the traveler have in the world according to the opening of the passage?
questions.answer: He is a guest trying to understand who sent him here.

questions.question: What does the atmosphere promise to help him discover?
questions.answer: The one he is seeking.

questions.question: How does the passage balance the description of the atmosphere’s appearance and behavior?
questions.answer: It seems rough in one way, yet it acts kindly and helpfully.

questions.question: What are some merciful effects of the clouds on earth?
questions.answer: They bring water, support life, cool things when needed, and rush help to places in need.

questions.question: What change in the clouds shows quick obedience?
questions.answer: They may disappear entirely and then gather again very fast when rain is commanded.

questions.question: Why is the gathering of clouds in a short time important in the passage?
questions.answer: It highlights speed, order, and control rather than randomness.

questions.question: What does the traveler conclude from the way the air behaves?
questions.answer: He concludes that it is serving under the command of the ruler of the universe.

questions.question: How is the air shown to be useful in everyday life?
questions.answer: It helps with breathing, brings needed energy, carries sound, and supports plant growth.

questions.question: What picture is given of the raindrops themselves?
questions.answer: They are shown as fine, shining, sweet drops filled with blessings.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying mercy seems to take form in rain?
questions.answer: It means Allah’s care becomes visible through the falling rain.

questions.question: What does the traveler do before thinking about lightning and thunder?
questions.answer: He first studies the clouds, the wind, and the rain.

questions.question: How are thunder and lightning connected to the rest of the passage?
questions.answer: They are presented as more examples of natural forces working with purpose.

questions.question: If a student said the passage is only about weather science, what important point would be missing?
questions.answer: The main point that these signs lead the traveler to recognize Allah’s wisdom, power, and mercy.

questions.question: In this passage, what does the atmosphere seem to do for the traveler?
questions.answer: It acts like a guide pointing him toward the truth he is searching for.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice when he pays attention to the atmosphere?
questions.answer: He notices powerful sounds and many meaningful events taking place in it.

questions.question: According to the passage, how do clouds help the world?
questions.answer: They nourish the earth, bring water for life, and help create good conditions for living things.

questions.question: What does the passage say clouds do when they are not visible?
questions.answer: Their parts withdraw so completely that they seem to leave no trace.

questions.question: What does their sudden return teach the traveler?
questions.answer: It teaches him that they move under command, not by themselves.

questions.question: How is the air described in terms of its service?
questions.answer: It is shown as a generous and wise worker with many duties.

questions.question: What is remarkable about the way the passage describes the atoms of air?
questions.answer: They are described as if each one were carefully receiving and carrying out instructions.

questions.question: Which needs of living things are met through the work of the air?
questions.answer: Breathing, warmth, light, energy, hearing, and plant pollination.

questions.question: How are raindrops presented as more than ordinary water?
questions.answer: They are presented as carriers of many gifts and signs of mercy.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect rain so strongly with compassion?
questions.answer: Because rain brings benefit gently and generously to creation.

questions.question: What brief point is made about lightning and thunder at the end of the target passage?
questions.answer: They too are assigned amazing tasks.

questions.question: What method does the passage use to teach the reader about Allah’s signs?
questions.answer: It has the traveler observe parts of nature and draw meaning from them.

questions.question: What is the strongest overall conclusion from the whole passage?
questions.answer: The atmosphere and its events show deliberate planning, mercy, and power from Allah.
